reason: adm-zip 0.5.12 memory-exhaustion on a crafted ZIP, pulled into word-addin only by office-addin-debugging/office-addin-manifest (devDependencies used to sideload the add-in on a developer's machine). Never bundled by webpack, never part of the shipped task pane, and the only ZIPs it opens are the manifest bundles we produce ourselves. npm's only 'fix' is a downgrade to office-addin-debugging 4.6.7, outside the declared ^5.0.12 range. REMOVE WHEN: the office-addin-* chain ships adm-zip >=0.6.0 inside that range (the weekly dev-dep Dependabot bump will carry it).

tmp 0.0.33 path traversal via prefix/postfix, reachable in word-addin only through @inquirer/editor -> external-editor, i.e. the interactive prompts of @microsoft/teamsapp-cli under office-addin-debugging — a devDependency, and the prefixes are literals inside that CLI rather than anything this repo or a document supplies. Same downgrade-only 'fix' as adm-zip above. REMOVE WHEN: external-editor resolves tmp >0.2.5 (or the teamsapp-cli chain drops external-editor) inside office-addin-debugging's declared range.

sharp 0.35.2 bundles a libheif with two HEIF-decoding CVEs (GHSA-g89c-p67h-r497, GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545). The vulnerable copy is the one miniflare pins EXACTLY (miniflare -> sharp 0.35.2), reached in the frontend only through wrangler, i.e. the local Cloudflare emulator behind `wrangler dev` / `opennextjs-cloudflare preview` on a developer's machine. It is not part of the deployed Worker or the Next.js bundle; the sharp that Next itself uses for image optimisation is already 0.35.4 (patched). No in-range fix exists: miniflare@latest (5.20260908.0-alpha, shipped by wrangler 4.130.0) still pins 0.35.2, and the pin is exact so npm update cannot move it. REMOVE WHEN: `npm view miniflare dependencies.sharp` reports >=0.35.4 and the frontend's wrangler resolves that miniflare (the weekly dev-dep Dependabot bump will carry it).
